title: Write an Issue
bottom_line: Type the command with a description of work you want done later. It opens a GitHub issue labeled `ai` and gives you its link.

sections.heading: Run it with a description of the work for later

blocks.code: /plan-tools:write-issue <description of the work to do later> [--label <name>]
blocks.caption: The description is required. The label is optional.

blocks.title: What you can pass
rows: Description of the work to do later
The command derives the issue's short title from it and writes the body from it and the conversation.
Uses `<name>` instead of `ai` as the label on the issue. Without it, the label is `ai`.

before.label: You type
before.text: fix null check in auth middleware

after.label: Issue title
after.text: Fix null check in auth middleware

blocks.caption: The command derives a short title from what you typed.

blocks.text: A typical case is a bug found during review that is out of scope for the current PR. You record it now and pick it up later.

sections.heading: You need the GitHub CLI signed in with push access

cards.title: git installed
cards.text: The plugin needs `git` alongside the GitHub CLI.

cards.title: GitHub CLI signed in
cards.text: Install `gh` and sign in with `gh auth login`, with push access to the repository. Every issue, PR and status command goes through `gh`.

sections.heading: Five steps take your sentence to a finished issue

steps.title: Makes sure the label exists
steps.text: If the `ai` label (or your `--label` name) is not in the repository yet, it creates it, with the description "Queued for autonomous implementation".

steps.title: Writes a short title
steps.text: It turns your description into a short title, for example `Fix null check in auth middleware`.

steps.title: Writes a self-contained body
steps.text: The body says what is wrong or needed, where (file and line if known), and any context from the current conversation that a future session would need to act on it without working it out again.

steps.title: Creates the issue
steps.text: It opens the issue on GitHub with that title, body and label.

steps.title: Gives you the link
steps.text: You should see the new issue's URL in the reply.

sections.heading: It only records the work and never starts it

cards.title: Records the work
cards.text: One labeled GitHub issue, ready to be picked up and done later.

cards.title: Does not implement it
cards.text: The command makes no code changes. It only records the work for later.

blocks.title: The same `ai` label is shared across the plugin
rows: Deferred work goes into GitHub issues labeled `ai`

blocks.text: Later, `/plan-tools:impl-issue` picks up `ai`-labeled issues. `/plan-tools:finalize-pr` also calls this command once for each big leftover item.

next_action.text: Type `/plan-tools:write-issue` followed by one sentence describing the work you want done later.
next_action.detail: Add `--label <name>` if you want a label other than `ai`.
